transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. It is very likely damaged and must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it. Running a microwave empty for ten minutes usually scorches internal components like the waveguide cover or paint, which causes that burning smell. Please switch it off at the wall and unplug it before doing anything else. With it unplugged, you can look inside to see if there is any blackened damage on the side panel or debris in the cavity. Do not try to run it again to test if the smell has gone away.

I'd only turned it off at the switch, so I'll unplug it now. There was some smoke coming out of the side vents when we stopped it, and the smell was a hot electrical one. Inside, there's a brownish mark on the panel on the side wall, and the cavity is empty. Is it safe to keep, or should I just bin it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If there are flames or smoke is still coming from it, keep away, don't open the door of an oven, microwave or dryer that is on fire, switch it off at the wall or the fuse box only if you can do that safely, get everyone out and call 999.

There are no flames and the smoke has stopped, it's unplugged now, though the smell is still faintly there half an hour later. So is it worth getting it checked, or is it a £60 microwave I should just bin?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If there are flames or smoke is still coming from it, keep away, don't open the door of an oven, microwave or dryer that is on fire, switch it off at the wall or the fuse box only if you can do that safely, get everyone out and call 999.

reading.symptom: horrible smell after running empty for 10 minutes

plan: They asked: "Is it broken?" - answer that first.

Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "horrible smell after running empty for 10 minutes". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply.
